{full} steps up, a {hcp} handicapper with great faith in a brand new driver.

To the {n}. Par {p}, {yd} yards, and a stiff breeze, I'm told.
fairway: Right down the middle. Nothing to see here, which is rather the point.
Lovely. That's found the short stuff.
Fairway. The greenkeeper will be thrilled someone is using it.
On the fairway, and a quiet nod of satisfaction.

A touch wayward. The rough here has swallowed better players.
Into the thick stuff, where good scores go to think things over.

Bunker. From up here it looks like a fried egg.

Sand. The architect will be quietly delighted.

In the water. Penalty stroke and a long walk to the drop.
Wet. Very wet. The ducks have scattered.
Gone in the drink. Character building, I believe they call it.

Into the timber. It's come down somewhere, I think.
Trees. Forty years in this game and I've never seen one move out of the way.
Woodland. Lovely for a walk, less so for a golf ball.

Over the fence. Stroke and distance, and a long face.
Oh, that's gone. Somebody's greenhouse may be in trouble.

That's on. Lovely flight on it, too.

Left it short. Never up, never in, as my old pro used to say, endlessly.
Tickled past. Tap in to come, hopefully.

A birdie, and a grin to go with it.

Well. We'll draw a veil over that one.

wx_sun: Glorious morning. Not a cloud. The bar will do a roaring trade later.
Sunshine. Shirtsleeves weather, and the course is buzzing.
wx_cloud: Grey skies, nothing worse. Perfectly decent golfing weather.
Overcast. The kind of day the British were built for.
wx_rain: Rain. Proper rain. Only the truly committed are out today.
Wet one. The greenkeepers are looking at the sky and muttering.

Storm. Nobody sensible is out, and the greenkeeper is watching the shoreline with a face like thunder.
wx_wind: Blowing a gale. Anything off the tee could end up in the next parish.
Windy. The flags are standing straight out. Club up and pray.

column: I once watched a man take eleven in a bunker and then thank the bunker. That's golf, really.
Somebody asked me what makes a great course. Good drainage and a decent bacon roll. Next question.
The wind is the finest golf architect who ever lived. Unpaid, unreliable and entirely unrepentant.
Members' committees are like weather fronts. You can see them coming and there is nothing whatsoever you can do.
Auctions are just golf with money. Everyone thinks they can go a bit further than they actually can.
There's no such thing as bad weather, only the wrong waterproofs and an empty car park.
The sea has been redesigning links courses for a thousand years. It has never once asked for planning permission.
